# Aegis by Clarvix

> External cybersecurity exposure assessment for small and mid-size businesses and solo founders in Israel. Aegis discovers what's publicly exposed about a business online, explains the real risk in plain language, and verifies the fix — including a built-in readiness check against Amendment 13 of Israel's Privacy Protection Law.

Aegis is a service by Clarvix. It is a passive, external security assessment — it does not perform active exploitation, phishing, or denial-of-service testing. Every automated finding is reviewed by a person before it reaches the client.

## Service

- Fixed price: ₪1,990, one-time.
- Includes: domain and subdomain discovery, email authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC), TLS/certificate check, public website and CMS review, exposed secrets and API key checks (relevant to apps built with AI tools like Lovable, Base44, Replit, on Supabase/Firebase), Amendment 13 privacy-law readiness check, executive and technical report, one retest.
- Delivery: 2–5 business days.
- Does not include: active exploitation, penetration testing with credential attacks, phishing simulations, or any action that could disrupt production systems.

## Audience

- Israeli SMBs (roughly 10–100 employees) with no in-house security lead.
- Solo founders and indie hackers who launched a product with AI coding tools and want it checked for common misconfigurations.

## Sourced claims on this site

Every statistic on the site is attributed and linked. For reference:

- Amendment 13 to Israel's Privacy Protection Law has been in force since 14 August 2025; the grace period for appointing a privacy officer ended 31 October 2025. The Privacy Protection Authority can impose administrative fines directly, without a court: up to 5% of annual turnover, capped at ₪140,000/year for smaller businesses. Source: IAPP.
- In July 2026 the Authority issued the first administrative fine under Amendment 13 — ₪256,000 — for late reporting of a data security incident. Source: Pearl Cohen.
- A Symbiotic Security scan of 1,072 vibe-coded apps found that 98% had at least one security flaw. Source: Symbiotic Security.
- In July 2025, Wiz Research found an authentication bypass in the Base44 platform allowing SSO to be bypassed on private apps using only the publicly visible app_id. Patched within 24 hours. Source: Wiz Research.
- IBM's Cost of a Data Breach 2025 puts the average time to identify a breach at 158 days, plus 83 days to contain it. Source: IBM.
